title: setup instructions --yes then --remove --yes gives back the original bytes of the file, whatever it ended with
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D8 (setup instructions, defect N-18): a delimited, reversible JITSO block in the instruction files agents read
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-18, setup instructions). For each original (empty, no final line break, a final line break, CRLF, a block quoted inside a fenced code block, a lone BEGIN inside a tilde fence, a final blank line, a single line break), the first run adds the block recording in `added=` how many line breaks it put before it, and `--remove --yes` deletes the block lines and exactly that many breaks, so the file equals its original again. Markers inside a fenced code block are not real markers. The oracle has no `setup` command: it answers `unknown command "setup"` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so every expectation that needs this output or file effect FAILS on it.
